title: Cross-family canonical obstruction atlas for failed 42 -> 43 extensions
novelty_claim: The missing Ramsey object is a reusable atlas of canonical minimal obstruction cores explaining failed orbit-distinct 42 -> 43 extensions across nonisomorphic parent families. If those cores transfer under an anti-Exoo holdout and remain witness-safe, the result is a new structural object rather than another OVE catalog, witness re-verification note, or optimizer variant.
closest_prior_art: Study of Exoo's Lower Bound for Ramsey number R(5,5) (Ge et al., 2022)
Can genetic algorithms with the symmetric heuristic find the Ramsey number R(5,5) (Aija'am, 2010)
differentiation: This route is only novel if the recurring cores survive canonical relabeling, family balance, and leave-one-parent-out transfer. The claim is not better search, lower defect, or extension emptiness itself; it is transfer-safe obstruction structure that can later be reused as pruning logic or proof-side lemmas.
easiest_falsifier: Kill immediately if the top canonical cores fail to cover at least 30 percent of orbit-distinct failed extensions across at least 3 parent families, if anti-Exoo held-out coverage falls below 50 percent of in-family coverage, or if any promoted core deletes a known 42- or 43-vertex witness.
evidence_plan: Blocker first: materialize `frontier_parent`, `extension_case`, and `failure_witness` records for at least 3 non-isomorphic parent families using existing repo tooling only; freeze one anti-Exoo holdout family and the saved witness set; canonicalize failure cores; run raw-versus-canonical, family-balance, and leave-one-parent-out audits; then test whether any surviving cores replay as witness-safe pruning lemmas or proof-side stubs.
budget_envelope: Champion only. Authorize one narrow Rung 0/1 atlas pilot, one anti-Exoo transfer audit, and one witness-safety audit. No wide search refresh, no new solver development, and no broader compute until recurrence and transfer survive.

title: Witness-safe orbit-quotient abstract state for Ramsey pruning
novelty_claim: A sound abstract state over orbit-labeled degree-matrix and joint-neighborhood bundle signatures could become the first reusable witness-safe bridge between lower-bound extension failures and upper-bound necessary-condition pruning in this workspace. The claim is a proof-auditable abstract layer, not another bag of filters.
closest_prior_art: Angeltveit-McKay upper-bound line culminating in R(5,5) <= 46 (2024)
Gauthier 2025 split-vertex / transverse-edge gluing strategy surface
Degree-matrix abstraction and cheap admissibility filtering in smaller exact Ramsey computations
differentiation: This route stays alive only if the abstract domain, concretization map, and refinement rules are explicit and sound. That separates it from ad hoc filter banks, from the current repo's cheap degree or neighborhood screens, and from static-analysis branding layered on the same decomposition without a replayable Ramsey state object.
easiest_falsifier: Kill if the abstract layer deletes any known 42- or 43-vertex witness, or if matched ablations show no measurable pre-decomposition shrinkage once the representation, solver, and proof logging are held fixed.
evidence_plan: After H1 exposes stable obstruction signatures, define the abstract domain on degree-matrix plus joint-neighborhood bundle types, specify concretization and monotone refinement, audit witness survival on the saved witness set, and benchmark the abstract layer on a solved rung or reconstructed frontier packet with the layer toggled on versus off under matched conditions.
budget_envelope: Backup only, and gated on H1 producing stable signatures. Authorize one narrow soundness audit and one matched ablation run. Stop on the first witness loss or stale-baseline failure. Do not market this as a standalone bound improvement until it yields a replayable lemma path.

title: Decomposition-primitive replacement beyond split-vertex and transverse-edge gluing
novelty_claim: The upper-bound bottleneck may be the decomposition primitive rather than the solver. A genuinely non-equivalent pair or shell decomposition that reduces verified residue or checked proof cost would constitute a real upper-bound-side advance.
closest_prior_art: A new upper bound on the Ramsey number R(5,5) (McKay and Radziszowski, 1992)
Decreasing the upper bound on the Ramsey number R(5,5) (Gauthier, 2025)
differentiation: This route survives only if it proves non-equivalence to the McKay-Radziszowski / Angeltveit-McKay / Gauthier split-glue surface before benchmarking. Solver shopping, branch-order changes, or residue reductions without a certificate advantage do not count as novelty.
easiest_falsifier: Kill if non-equivalence cannot be demonstrated on a solved smaller rung, or if primitive-only matched benchmarks fail to improve verified residue size, proof bytes, or checker runtime over the existing split/glue baseline.
evidence_plan: Specify one to three candidate primitives such as adjacent-pair, nonadjacent-pair, or small-shell decompositions; prove or empirically certify non-equivalence on a verified ladder rung; then run primitive-on versus primitive-off benchmarks with solver, proof format, preprocessing, thread count, warm starts, and cached clauses fixed.
budget_envelope: Tertiary fallback only. Spend zero effort here until H1 and H1B are killed or explicitly deprioritized. If opened, fund one small matched benchmark ladder before any n = 45 residue work and stop immediately on overlap or certificate-path failure.
